Flagship case study 01: sustaining the cementless (porous) knee system and platform DCR campaign

A complete lifecycle overview of sustaining engineering, cross-functional change control and post-clearance release management for a high-mix commercial orthopedic platform.

1. Context and scope

Conformis/restor3d introduced an architectural update to its patient-specific knee system, incorporating a cement-free (porous) biological fixation variant with 3D additive gyroid lattice structures. The challenge was moving the new design inputs into full-scale production while sustaining active commercial case turnaround across four interlinked teams: CAD Design, Manufacturing, Process Engineering and Quality Assurance.

2. The sustaining challenge

  • Interface discrepancies between updated additive implant geometry and patient-specific surgical jigs (PSI).
  • 571 open JIRA items spanning functional CAD modeling bugs, tolerance stack-ups and shop-floor improvement suggestions.
  • The need for rapid design fixes without halting daily custom implant delivery or introducing secondary regressions.

3. Engineering strategy and execution

  • Closed-loop feedback triage: Established a central triage protocol in JIRA and categorized all 571 tickets into CAD bugs, manufacturing frame limitations, routing updates and design/process improvement suggestions, evaluating each against surgical lead-time constraints.
  • Grouped DCR campaign architecture: Replaced sporadic, high-risk one-off releases by consolidating interdependent fixes into 4 controlled Design Change Requests (DCRs).
  • Cross-attribute verification protocol: A mandatory pre-release rule: any single geometry or tolerance fix was tested across all mating assembly models within the DCR package, so no change created secondary downstream conflicts.
  • Shop-floor handover: Personally governed file handoffs after release, verifying that CNC and additive manufacturing cells received frozen, validated CAD/CAM datasets, tooling prints and updated Work Instructions (WIs).

4. Measurable outcomes

  • 571 JIRA tickets closed: Resolved 100% of reported CAD bugs and continuous improvement suggestions across 4 functional departments.
  • Rapid resolution cadence: Delivered and validated each DCR release package in an average of ~2 weeks.
  • Zero production regressions: 100% first-pass yield on all DCR-released updates, with zero production line stoppages or field complaints.
  • DHF compliance: Updated all design outputs, PFMEAs and inspection criteria directly in the Design History File (DHF).

Flagship case study 02: engineering governance and automated quality verification

How I scale design quality across 16 engineers and reduce pre-release human error through custom SolidWorks automation.

1. Dual-team operational leadership

  • Initial Process / Segmentation Team (9 engineers): Reconstructing 3D anatomical models (femur, tibia, hip) from patient DICOM CT datasets and establishing the mechanical axes and reference planes fundamental to patient-matched design.
  • Implant & PSI Design Team (7 engineers): Engineering patient-specific femoral/tibial implants and single-use surgical resection cutting jigs.
  • Governance model: Standardized daily workload allocation, ran technical gate reviews, mentored engineers on complex parametric modeling, and enforced adherence to approved design inputs.

2. The verification bottleneck

High-volume custom implant production requires rigorous pre-release checks on every assembly: anatomical boundary fit, jig slot clearance, pin guide trajectory and mating clearances. Doing these checks manually across dozens of cases a day created inspection fatigue, risk of human oversight and longer case cycle times.

3. Automated solution: SolidWorks assembly review macro

I built and deployed an automated SolidWorks review macro that runs objective design-rule verification before senior engineer sign-off:

  • Automated loading: The macro programmatically loads the completed patient assembly into an isolated review session.
  • Multi-point geometry audit: Systematically checks predefined critical zones: interference detection, cutting slot width tolerances, boundary envelope limits and feature-tree suppression states.
  • Traceable quality output: Generates an external, timestamped HTML verification report marking every evaluated parameter PASS or FAIL.

4. Impact and audit readiness

  • Accelerated review velocity: Cut manual CAD assembly review time significantly across the department.
  • Standardized gatekeeping: Removed subjective reviewer bias: every case is evaluated against identical, deterministic engineering thresholds.
  • Quality traceability: The HTML reports serve as clean objective verification records supporting internal quality audits.

Design control and quality case studies

CAPA: build envelope exceedance in additive manufacturing

  • The non-conformance: Pre-production manufacturing validation detected select patient-specific implant CAD models exceeding the physical build envelope of the manufacturing frame/tray.
  • Root cause analysis: Extreme patient anatomical variability (99th percentile sizing) combined with insufficient bounding-box perimeter constraints in the primary CAD seed template.
  • Containment: Audited all in-process and pending production orders and quarantined 100% of affected CAD models immediately, preventing scrap.
  • Corrective and preventive action: Updated the PFMEA to include extreme anatomical dimensions as an evaluated failure mode; embedded hard bounding-box constraints in CAD seed templates and published updated design review Work Instructions; validated the updated process against extreme anatomical edge cases per formal V&V protocols.
  • Outcome: Closed with formal approvals from Quality, CAD and Manufacturing. Zero non-conforming units reached the operating floor.

NCR: critical mating feature omission on a surgical resection jig

  • Detection: Incoming QA inspection identified an omitted fillet on a critical mating surface of a patient-specific resection guide.
  • Investigation and containment: Traced the root cause to an unlinked parametric suppression state during automated 3D file export. Quarantined all active files in the lot.
  • Disposition and DHF update: Initiated the NCR and a controlled CAD Rework Form, corrected the master feature tree, verified mating tolerances, re-released validated files and compiled objective evidence into the DHF.
  • Outcome: Remediated and released on schedule; an isolated one-off with no systemic trend, closed with zero production downtime.

Process deviation: custom partitioning for oversized tooling

  • Scenario: A patient's unique anatomical deformity required surgical guide geometry that exceeded single-piece additive build dimensions.
  • Resolution: Formulated an approved, traceable process deviation to section the model into two interlocking, keyed STL sub-components.
  • Traceability and governance: Created the deviation authorization, updated the production traveler/router and completed verification checks in the DHF before physical production.
  • Outcome: Delivered patient-critical surgical tooling on schedule within approved regulatory risk boundaries.

Retrospective containment audits (5+ campaigns)

  • Scope: 5+ comprehensive containment audits covering 60 days of historical production across tibial implants, femoral resection jigs and tooling drawings.
  • Result: 100% containment integrity: zero non-compliant devices escaped to hospital inventory or clinical users.
